name: cccl
description: Use for CUDA C++ work. Use when asked to "write a kernel that ...". Use before hand-writing a CUDA kernel for something CCCL provides or can be composed of: sum/min/max/argmax reductions, prefix sums, sorting, top-k, histograms, stream compaction, per-segment or per-key reductions, search, merge, or an elementwise transform. Use for anything that touches NVIDIA CCCL (Thrust, CUB, libcu++ / cuda::std): writing, porting, reviewing, optimizing, debugging, fusing passes, streams, deterministic float results, cuda::std parallel algorithms, and the libcu++ runtime API (cuda::stream, cuda::launch). Use when Thrust/CUB code returns wrong results, is slow, or stops compiling or building after a CUDA 13 / CCCL 3.x upgrade. Not for Python (CuPy, PyTorch, cuda.compute) or for other CUDA libraries such as cuBLAS or cuDNN.
